Formally, mer_overgen_exceeds_one_witness confirms unbounded normalized edit distance, while bounded_mer_always_unit_bounded only bounds raw edits, not the MER ratio. Effective only with cap/mer_bnd hardening.
models.mcs_assessment: Empirically discriminative (Cohen_d=6.42; aligned-index recovery 54.5 pp) but collapses under index shift (mcsMatches=0 witness) and exhibits 51.9 pp corpus/sentence denominator bias (truncation_asymmetry: mcs_corpus=1.0 vs mcs_idx=0.481). Effective with aligned-index recovery and fixed sentence-level denominator hardening.
models.uwec_assessment: Empirically weak (Cohen_d=0.36; OOD strict-parse gap 0.22 pp; values 0.37–0.93 across regimes without separation). Formally exposed by phi_inflation_without_fsa_validity: metric inflation without validity. Not effective as a standalone OOD measure.
models.key_evidence: MER and MCS show high Cohen_d (17.05, 6.42) but fail formal bounds (MER > 1; MCS shift collapse and denominator asymmetry). UWEC shows negligible OOD sensitivity (Cohen_d=0.36, 0.22 pp gap). Clean parse is only 40.89% with 31.81% diacritic words, indicating morphological complexity that raw metrics mishandle.
models.recommended_hardening: Cap MER at 1.0 (use mer_bnd); compute MCS with aligned-index and sentence-level denominator, rejecting negative shifts; do not use UWEC for OOD without strict-parse/OOD gating or replacement.
